name: FHHNC (CLDN16/CLDN19)
aliases: familial hypomagnesaemia with hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis

clinicalPearls: Autosomal recessive tubulopathy caused by variants in CLDN16 (paracellin-1) or CLDN19, tight-junction claudins of the thick ascending limb
Defined by the triad of renal magnesium wasting causing hypomagnesaemia, hypercalciuria, and bilateral nephrocalcinosis
Unlike most hypomagnesaemic tubulopathies, urinary calcium excretion is high rather than low, driving stone formation and calcium deposition
A distinguishing feature is progression to chronic kidney disease, often reaching kidney failure in adolescence or early adulthood
CLDN19 disease additionally causes ocular abnormalities such as severe myopia, nystagmus, and macular colobomata
Management focuses on magnesium supplementation, measures to reduce hypercalciuria (such as thiazide diuretics and generous fluids), and monitoring of renal function
Suspect FHHNC in a child with recurrent stones or nephrocalcinosis, hypomagnesaemia, and hypercalciuria, and confirm with CLDN16/CLDN19 testing
reference.pathophysiology: In the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle, magnesium and calcium are reabsorbed passively through the paracellular pathway, driven by a lumen-positive transepithelial voltage. Claudin-16 and claudin-19 form the tight-junction complex that creates this selective divalent-cation channel. Loss-of-function variants abolish paracellular magnesium and calcium reabsorption, so both ions are lost in the urine, producing hypomagnesaemia and hypercalciuria. The persistently high urinary calcium precipitates as nephrocalcinosis and stones, and chronic interstitial injury from calcium deposition, together with the primary transport defect, drives progressive decline in glomerular filtration towards kidney failure. Claudin-19 is also expressed in the eye, accounting for the ocular manifestations of that subtype.
additionalDifferentials: Distal renal tubular acidosis with nephrocalcinosis
Dent disease and other causes of hypercalciuric nephrolithiasis
additionalInvestigations: Serum magnesium and calcium with fractional excretion of magnesium confirming renal loss
24-hour or spot urinary calcium demonstrating hypercalciuria
Renal ultrasound documenting medullary nephrocalcinosis and stones
Serial estimated glomerular filtration rate to track progression
Ophthalmological assessment where CLDN19 disease is suspected
redFlags: Rising creatinine indicating progression to chronic kidney disease
Obstructing calculi or recurrent urinary tract infection
Symptomatic hypomagnesaemia with tetany or seizures
Rapidly worsening vision in CLDN19 disease
reference.prognosis: The outlook is guarded because of the strong tendency to progressive chronic kidney disease, with many patients reaching kidney failure by early adulthood; magnesium supplementation corrects symptoms but does not halt renal decline, and CLDN19 disease carries additional visual morbidity.
pitfalls: Confusing FHHNC with Gitelman syndrome, which shows hypocalciuria rather than hypercalciuria
Assuming magnesium replacement will prevent progression to renal failure
Overlooking nephrocalcinosis on imaging in a child investigated for hypomagnesaemia
Failing to arrange ophthalmological review when CLDN19 is implicated
management: Provide chronic oral magnesium replacement for renal magnesium wasting, titrated to symptom control rather than full biochemical normalisation
Use thiazide diuretics with high fluid intake and citrate or alkali supplementation to reduce hypercalciuria and slow nephrocalcinosis
Institute nephroprotective management of declining glomerular filtration, including blood-pressure and proteinuria control and avoidance of nephrotoxins
Give parenteral magnesium for acute neuromuscular manifestations such as tetany or seizures
Arrange ophthalmological review where CLDN19 disease is suspected, monitoring severe myopia and macular disease
Offer renal replacement therapy or transplantation for kidney failure, which cures the intrinsic tubular transport defect
Provide genetic counselling with CLDN16 and CLDN19 sequencing and screening of siblings, given autosomal recessive inheritance
